title.narrative: Activity under preparation Enhancing maritime security and safety of navigation in the Southern Red Sea, Horn of Africa and Gulf of Aden region (Red Sea-HoA Programme II)

description.narrative: The Red Sea and Gulf of Aden form a key maritime route for international trade, where a single disruptive event, such as conflict or a shipping accident, can significantly impact trade and transport. Historically, the region has been plagued by piracy and remains a corridor for illicit trafficking, including arms, people smuggling, and potential terrorist movements between the African and Arabian Peninsula coasts. The strategic landscape shifted dramatically following the numerous Houthi attacks targeting shipping vessels and tanks, further highlighting the region's vulnerabilities. Due to these attacks, shipping through the Red Sea has fallen by 70% since the beginning of 2024 Many vessels now detour around the Cape of Good Hope, adding 3,500 nautical miles, 16 to 32 days, and nearly EUR 900K in costs per journey. European shipping companies rerouted the vast majority of Asia¿Europe loops during peak months, implying an effective 60¿75% reduction in container services using the Red Sea in 2024, with avoidance persisting well into 2025The Action intends to build on the results of the first phase of the programme (11th EDF - Regional Programme for Maritime Security in the Red Sea Area, ending in November 2026), adapting the intervention logic and the activities to the new security and geo-political scenario, with the overall objective of enhancing maritime security and safety of navigation in the Southern Red Sea and Gulf of Aden region, with a specific focus on Somalia, Djibouti, Ethiopia, Sudan and Yemen. This subject was identified in Priority Area 2 (Democratic Governance, Peace and Security, Culture), Specific Objective 2 (Peace and Security) of the Multi-Annual Indicative Programme for Sub-Saharan Africa 2021-2027. The Action is in line with SDG 16 - Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions and DAC Markers on maritime security and trafficking, legal and judicial development, advanced technical and managerial training, and governance.Contributing to the implementation of the EU¿s policy and priorities under its maritime security strategies, the Strategic Compass, and the Global Gateway, the Action will contribute to: (i) strengthening national maritime law enforcement agencies to efficiently prevent, repress and respond to maritime threats and related hybrid menaces; (ii) enhancing capacities and capabilities of maritime affairs and port authorities in terms of port security and safety of navigation standards; (iii) strengthening intra and inter-regional maritime domain awareness (MDA); and (iv) reinforcing national judicial capacities to establish or improve the legal finish mechanism.To achieve the overall objective, an integrated approach will be applied, covering capacity building and mentoring, and promoting communication and coordination among national, international and regional partners, including the private sector. The Action will be carried out in complementarity with both EU and non-EU funded actions at national and regional level, and in cooperation with relevant Regional Economic Communities and other regional stakeholders.
